gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1173g:
Auditing federal books is guided by a joint manual, updated here as GAO-07-1173G, dated August 28, 2007. The Financial Audit Manual is kept by GAO and the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency. Volume Three is the part issued in this update.

The manual tells auditors how to run financial statement audits of federal bodies. It is a key tool for answerability over taxpayer funds. Auditors use its steps to test if agency books are fair and if controls work. For readers, the volume shows the craft rules behind every clean, or unclean, opinion on a federal balance sheet. It is a working text, not a report of findings.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-313g: Federal financial audits follow a shared manual kept by GAO and an inspectors general council. GAO-07-313G, dated June 29, 2007, is the exposure draft of that manual's third volume. The Financial Audit Manual guides audits of federal bodies' financial statements. It is a core tool for holding agencies to account for taxpayer funds. An exposure draft is a proposed text put out for comment before final issue.
podcast-joerogan-TZqADzuu73g:
Former CIA officer John Kiriakou joins Joe Rogan for episode 2392 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Kiriakou was the first official to confirm the agency's waterboarding program on the record. He later served prison time for leaking a name, a price he calls a patriot's burden.

Kiriakou describes the torture debate inside the agency and the fallout that followed his disclosure. He shares his wider view of the CIA's sins and habits since. Rogan asks what real reform would take and whether it is possible. Principled and curious listeners get a whistleblower's account in full.
podcast-tuckercarlson-xTAJnJUos3g:
Investor Kevin O'Leary debates Tucker Carlson on AI, American jobs, and the fate of the American empire in this episode. O'Leary, famous from Shark Tank, defends markets and the tech boom with a businessman's faith. Carlson takes the populist side, and sparks fly between them.

The two argue over whether AI will enrich workers or replace them by the millions. They clash on trade, China, and whether America's best days are behind it. O'Leary answers with numbers and deal logic, Carlson with culture and nation. Concerned viewers get a real debate, not an interview, on the country's economic future.
podcast-tuckercarlson-y79CfG2R_3g:
Tucker Carlson reports from the ground on what life is truly like for Christians in the Holy Land. The episode title promises the real tale, not the press line. Carlson builds the report from talks with Christians who live there.

Carlson shares their tales of blocked rites, seized homes, and fear in old towns. He argues the land's first faith is being squeezed out while the West funds the squeeze. He asks why US churches keep so still. Listeners get a field report that cuts hard against the grain. The library keeps it as a record of his stated case.
